title: TargetSlotsContainer
description: The slots.json container (E4, B37/D23): formalizes what B25 deliberately left informal, because P9's write-back depends on it (B26 — 'the cells come from the slots'). Wraps the parsed TargetSlot[] with the parse provenance that binds cells to the exact source file. Each slots[] item is validated against the FROZEN target-slot.schema.json by the writer (engine/planning/plan.py validates every slot before writing; enforced by tests/planning) — the container schema deliberately does not duplicate the frozen per-slot contract.

source_mode.description: How the structure arrived (parse.py owns the vocabulary; currently client_provided).

parser_version.description: The parser that produced these slots — a re-parse under a newer parser is a different container.

source_sha256.description: Digest of the buyer file the slots were parsed from — the write-back binding: cells may only be written into a copy of THIS file.

slot_count.description: Must equal len(slots) — the honest-count guard the writer enforces.

slots.description: TargetSlot objects, each schema-valid against target-slot.schema.json (frozen, CLAUDE.md rule 3) — validated per-item by the writer, not re-specified here.

sources.description: P16 (mixed target sets): one entry per parsed target file when the declared set has MORE than one. Absent on single-target containers — their shape is byte-pinned pre-P16. When present, the top-level source_sha256 is the FIRST declared target's digest and write-back consults this list to bind each slot's file to its exact source.
